Mullaghmore

Mullach Mór

A distinctive, terraced limestone hill rising from the heart of Burren National Park, its concentric grey rings visible for miles around. The Irish name simply means "the big summit."

Unlike much of the surrounding karst, Mullaghmore's slopes feed a turlough — a seasonal lake that fills and empties through underground drainage — making the hill a study in how water shapes this landscape from both above and below ground.
